primary_intent: Ensure that Rosa Delgado (DOB 1979-06-14) has exactly one AllergyIntolerance for penicillin recorded in Medplum with the specified fields and values, creating it only if missing. A reasonable user would be inflexible about the correct patient match, correct SNOMED code, and required statuses; they would be flexible about whether the patient page itself was opened as long as the correct Patient reference is used and no duplicates are created.
reasoning: Nitpicks: The patient record wasn’t shown opened; the agent’s narrative mentions another Rosa’s allergy without on-screen proof (irrelevant to the target patient); and the agent provided narrative before the RESULT line. None affect the outcome. Critical issues: None—no wrong patient, no wrong code/values, and no duplicates for the target patient are evident. Critical-Point rule: SUCCESS — the agent crossed the save boundary and created the AllergyIntolerance correctly using provided info. Outcome analysis: Screenshot 1 shows two Rosa Delgados; the correct patient (DOB 1979-06-14) has ID Patient/1cb0381e-325d-406d-a991-df07181628da. Screenshot 2 confirms an AllergyIntolerance with id 17f4cad8-4afc-4af4-9566-8fb16c2666aa referencing that exact Patient, code system http://snomed.info/sct code 91936005, criticality high, clinicalStatus active (http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-clinical), and verificationStatus confirmed (http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-verification). Only the requested user-entered fields were set; id/meta are system-generated. There is no evidence of a duplicate for the 1979-06-14 patient. The RESULT line includes the correct resource id. The user’s primary intent is satisfied.
